title: Historical-37 recovery/adjudication closeout
objective: Re-examine the 37 programs the prior closeout (docs/validation/GLOBAL_FORMULAIC_ECONOMIC_COMPLETION_CLOSEOUT.json) classified GENERIC_AUTHORITY_BLOCKER, using ONLY existing retained project knowledge (no external web research), to determine whether their existing PARSED-tier data is substantively sufficient to calculate the economic benefit.
method: For each of the 37, read the existing DoctrineRecord/RateRule already on record (rate, min_spend, cap, conditions) and its citation text. All 37 already carried a real, non-null rate figure recorded by a prior research pass. Where a citation's own text described an apparent conflict (an old catalog figure vs a fresher secondary source, or 'carried forward unchallenged'), the original researcher had already adjudicated it down to ONE operative, calculable rate -- none of the 37 was found to have a genuine unresolved internal conflict between two live, competing figures. confidence_tier was deliberately left at PARSED for all 37 (no re-verification against an official primary source was performed this pass, per the no-web-research constraint) -- only the coverage veto was removed, since blocks_economic_candidacy() is independent of confidence_tier and the pricing engine (priceability()/get_rate_rules()) already accepts any tier.

data_quality_fix_found_during_recovery.issue: Its citation reads 'up to 40%' (a discretionary ceiling), but the existing RateRule tier had is_band_ceiling=False -- encoding it as a guaranteed flat 40% rate. Caught by test_no_still_priceable_program_encodes_an_up_to_maximum_as_a_flat_rate, which only checks non-blocked programs and had never evaluated this slug while it was vetoed. Corrected to is_band_ceiling=True with a disclosed condition, same treatment as every other 'up to X%' program in this registry.

recovery_summary.obsolete_coverage_vetoes_removed: 37 canonical rows + 28 alias-spelling duplicate rows = 65 total

test_suite: See git log for the exact pass/fail count at this commit.
